industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried; the condition ('to B if a source carries a healthcare read with the industry's relative strength holding A or B') is half met for a second week. Relative strength, 2026-11-13 against 2026-09-11, not week on week: A now, D prior, with Medtech capital goods A and Medtech consumables B; but no source spoke to healthcare, pharmaceuticals or medical technology this week (the Researcher's industry and sector reports are empty). Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). The view stays in the sector rows (Pharma/biotech and Hospitals Overweight, clinical-stage Biotech Underweight), because the industry letter would add the same weight to clinical-stage biotech (relative strength D) as to large pharma; 26 Pool stocks are healthcare and eight of the top 40 on the starting score. Counter-case for B: the market's chosen defensive on a second reading at A. To B when a source carries a healthcare read with relative strength still A or B.

sector.why: Overweight. Component 1 regime (rates-led late cycle: Richard's view 16-Sep-26, rates and yields rising, inflation high, consumer confidence low, downside skew; sources absent): non-discretionary demand, defensive earnings; relative strength AGREES, A both readings. Counter-case: three stocks, leveraged property-heavy operators are rate-sensitive.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Poland this week; Goldman's note (22 Oct) that emerging-market sovereign spreads are widening with US rate volatility is general, not Polish, and the condition for D (a source reading Polish spreads wider, or a third memo naming the sovereign) is not met; no memo carried a congruence line this week. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Twelve of the 149 Pool stocks are Polish, seven of them banks, so this is still the country row most likely to move. Relative strength is not graded by country.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
